### Electron Version

39.2.7

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

26.3

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

When the app is launched via a Universal Link (Associated Domains / applinks:), Electron should emit `continue-activity` and include the clicked URL in `details.webpageURL`, even on cold launch.

Example:

```js
app.on('continue-activity', (event, type, userInfo, details) => {
  console.log('continue-activity', { type, userInfo, details });
  // details.webpageURL should be the clicked https URL
});
```

This should work whether the app is already running or cold-launched.

### Actual Behavior

Universal Links only work if the app is already running.

If the app is running, `continue-activity` fires and `details.webpageURL` is populated.

If the app is fully quit, clicking a Universal Link launches the app, but no `continue-activity` event fires and the URL is lost.

### Testcase Gist URL

N/A — cannot be reproduced in Electron Fiddle. This requires macOS Associated Domains entitlements, code signing/notarization, and an HTTPS domain hosting a valid apple-app-site-association file. 

### Additional Information

Repro steps (requires a signed + notarized build with Associated Domains / applinks):

1. Sign + notarize an Electron app with `com.apple.developer.associated-domains` set to `applinks:<domain>`
2. Add an `app.on('continue-activity')` listener that logs `details.webpageURL`
3. Quit the app completely
4. Click a Universal Link for that domain in Safari
5. The app launches but `continue-activity` is not emitted

This appears to be caused by logic in [`shell/browser/mac/electron_application_delegate.mm`](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/shell/browser/mac/electron_application_delegate.mm).

Electron constructs `details` from `userActivity.webpageURL`, but returns early if `userActivity.userInfo` is nil:

```obj-c
NSURL* url = userActivity.webpageURL;
NSDictionary* details = url ? @{@"webpageURL" : url.absoluteString} : @{};

if (!userActivity.userInfo)
  return NO;
```

For Universal Links (`NSUserActivityTypeBrowsingWeb`), the URL is delivered via `webpageURL`, and `userInfo` is optional and often nil.

Apple documentation:

- `NSUserActivity.userInfo` is optional (`[AnyHashable: Any]?`) and may be nil:  
  https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/nsuseractivity/userinfo
- For `NSUserActivityTypeBrowsingWeb`, the URL is provided via `webpageURL`:  
  https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/nsuseractivity/webpageurl

Because Electron returns early when `userInfo` is nil, valid Universal Link activities (which only populate `webpageURL`) are dropped on cold launch.

A minimal fix would be to treat missing `userInfo` as an empty dictionary and still forward the activity:

```obj-c
NSDictionary* user_info = userActivity.userInfo ?: @{};
return browser->ContinueUserActivity(
           activity_type,
           electron::NSDictionaryToValue(user_info),
           electron::NSDictionaryToValue(details))
           ? YES : NO;
```

### Expected Behavior

After the renderer process crashes and the page is recovered via webContents.reload(), calling win.setIgnoreMouseEvents(true, { forward: true }) when the cursor is over the click-through area and win.setIgnoreMouseEvents(false) when it leaves should behave the same as before the crash: mouseenter/mouseleave fire only when the cursor actually enters or leaves the element, and the window correctly switches between click-through and normal mode. After a click in the click-through area, mouseleave should still fire when the cursor leaves, so the window can return to non–click-through state.

### Actual Behavior

After the renderer crashes and we call webContents.reload() in the render-process-gone handler:
When the cursor moves inside the click-through area, mouseenter and mouseleave fire repeatedly even though the cursor has not left the element, so the app repeatedly calls setIgnoreMouseEvents(true) and setIgnoreMouseEvents(false) and the window flickers between click-through and normal mode.
After one click in that area while it is in click-through mode, mouseleave stops firing. The window then stays in click-through mode and never returns to normal mode, so the user can no longer interact with the window.

nodes.body:

### Electron Version

41.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

MacOS all

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

40.4.1

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

Apps should be able to update using Squirrel.Mac without issue.

### Actual Behavior

Currently, our signed app is failing to update with the following errors:
```
Detected this as an install request
ERROR: Unrecognized attribute string flag '?' in attribute string "T@"NSString",?,R,C" for property debugDescription
ERROR: Unrecognized attribute string flag '?' in attribute string "T@"NSString",?,R,C" for property debugDescription
Installation error: Error Domain=SQRLShipItRequestErrorDomain Code=2 "Could not read update request" UserInfo={NSLocalizedDescription=Could not read update request, NSUnderlyingError=0x60000174aac0 {Error Domain=SQRLShipItRequestErrorDomain Code=1 "Missing required value" UserInfo={NSLocalizedDescription=Missing required value, NSLocalizedRecoverySuggestion="targetBundleURL" must not be set to nil.}}}
ShipIt quitting
```

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Ref https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/38437, which I think contains the breaking change.

My current theory is that the Mantle roll from 78d3966 → 2a8e212 changes how we're handling deserialization, and also  pulled in a new bug here (https://github.com/Mantle/Mantle/issues/899) - shout out to @CliftonH for the find!
One or both of the following are what I'm looking into:

1. `+propertyKeys` behavior changed: The old Mantle included all properties except readonly ones. The new Mantle delegates to `+storageBehaviorForPropertyWithKey:`, which adds `instancesRespondToSelector:` checks and recursive superclass lookups that can change which properties are included/excluded for Squirrel's SQRLShipItRequest.
2. `NSCoding` decode changed: `-decodeValueForKey:withCoder:modelVersion:` switched from NSInvocation-based dispatch to direct IMP calling, which could cause issues if method signatures don't match exactly.

The result is that targetBundleURL deserializes as nil, which is a required field, causing ShipIt to reject the update request and exit.

This was discovered while testing an Electron 40 → 41 upgrade. We currently don't test the updater with code-signed binaries, which is likely why this wasn't caught sooner.

nodes.title: fix: orphaned zygote enters infinite CPU spinloop on Linux (ENOTSOCK)
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

39.2.4

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Linux

### Operating System Version

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (Linux 6.8.0-101-generic, x86_64)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

When the main Electron process exits or restarts, orphaned zygote processes should either be terminated or detect the broken IPC socket and exit cleanly.

### Actual Behavior

When an Electron app crashes or restarts on Linux, orphaned zygote processes from the previous session can survive with broken IPC file descriptors. The zygote enters an infinite CPU spinloop, burning 80%+ of a core indefinitely and spamming error logs at ~4000 lines/second.

This same bug has been reported for VS Code: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/288893 — confirmed affecting multiple users on Ubuntu 24.04 across different Electron apps.

#### Root Cause

In `content/zygote/zygote_linux.cc`, `HandleRequestFromBrowser()` at line 243-245:

```cpp
if (len == -1) {
    PLOG(ERROR) << "Error reading message from browser";
    return false;  // ← returns to main loop
}
```

When the orphaned zygote's IPC fd (fd 3) points to a regular file instead of a socket, `RecvMsg()` returns -1 with `errno == ENOTSOCK`. The code correctly exits on EOF/ECONNRESET (line 235-240) but not on ENOTSOCK. Returning `false` goes back to `ProcessRequests()`'s main loop, where `ppoll()` on a regular file returns POLLIN immediately — creating the spinloop.

The orphaned zygote's fds after restart:
```
fd 3 -> /usr/lib/slack/icudtl.dat          (should be IPC socket)
fd 4 -> /usr/lib/slack/v8_context_snapshot.bin  (should be IPC socket)
```

Strace of the spinloop (~33,000 syscalls/second, zero backoff):
```
recvmsg(3, ...) = -1 ENOTSOCK
socketpair(AF_UNIX, SOCK_SEQPACKET, 0, [10, 11]) = 0
sendmsg(4, ..., cmsg_data=[11]) = -1 ENOTSOCK
write(2, "...ERROR:content/zygote/zygote_linux.cc:245] Error reading message
       from browser: Socket operation on non-socket (88)\n", 139) = 139
close(10); close(11); getpid()
# repeats immediately
```

#### Impact

- **CPU**: 83% of one core (single-threaded, R state)
- **Disk**: `~/.xsession-errors` grew to **15 GB** (111 million lines) in ~40 minutes
- **Persistent**: continues indefinitely until manually killed

#### Proposed Fix

Extend the existing exit path to cover non-recoverable socket errors:

```diff
--- a/content/zygote/zygote_linux.cc
+++ b/content/zygote/zygote_linux.cc
@@ -240,6 +240,14 @@ bool Zygote::HandleRequestFromBrowser(int fd) {
   }

   if (len == -1) {
+    // If the IPC socket fd is fundamentally invalid (not a socket, or bad fd),
+    // there is no way to recover. This happens when the zygote is orphaned
+    // after the browser process exits and restarts, leaving file descriptors
+    // pointing to non-socket files. Exit to avoid an infinite spinloop.
+    if (errno == ENOTSOCK || errno == EBADF) {
+      LOG(ERROR) << "Zygote IPC socket is invalid, exiting orphaned zygote";
+      _exit(0);
+    }
     PLOG(ERROR) << "Error reading message from browser";
     return false;
   }
```

This is a minimal, safe change: `ENOTSOCK`/`EBADF` are non-recoverable errors that indicate the fd is not a socket at all, so the zygote can never receive valid messages and should exit like it already does for EOF.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Observed in Slack 4.47.69 (Electron 39.2.4). The VS Code issue (microsoft/vscode#288893) confirms this affects the latest Electron versions as well, with VS Code 1.109.2 users reporting 70-100% CPU from orphaned zygote processes.

A full Electron patch file is also available at: https://gist.github.com/ (can be provided if helpful).

nodes.title: Allow different WebContents to reuse the renderer process for same-origin pages
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Currently, in Electron, when multiple WebContents instances load pages from the same domain, each one creates a separate SiteInstance and renderer process. This increases memory usage and can lead to inefficiencies, especially in applications that require opening many same-origin tabs or windows. By contrast, in Chromium's window.open scenario, the new WebContents reuses the opener's SiteInstance and can share a renderer process for the same-origin case, resulting in better resource sharing.

### Proposed Solution

Introduce a feature that allows developers to explicitly create or clone a WebContents in such a way that, when loading a same-origin page, its SiteInstance and renderer process can be reused. For example, providing an API similar to webContents.clone() or a dedicated option to share SiteInstance between WebContents, so that they behave more like window.open in the browser context and can share renderer processes when appropriate.

### Alternatives Considered

No reliable way is available to achieve process reuse for same-origin cases in Electron's public API.

### Additional Information

Sharing renderer processes for same-origin WebContents can improve memory efficiency and emulate browser behaviors more closely in Electron-based applications. This could enable advanced use cases, such as tabbed browsers and collaborative editors, while keeping system resource usage controlled.

After completing a drag and drop operation inside the application window, the app should continue working normally. I expect to still be able to click on UI elements, use keyboard shortcuts like Ctrl R, and interact with the window controls without any interruption.

### Actual Behavior

After performing a drag and drop action inside the window, the application becomes unresponsive to input. The window continues rendering and animations still play, and I can move or resize the window using the window manager. However, I can no longer click any UI elements, including the window controls, and keyboard shortcuts such as Ctrl R do not work. The problem appears after internal drag and drop actions inside the window, such as dragging a member entry within the UI. It may not trigger on the first attempt, but after several repetitions the window stops responding to input.

A short strace taken while the window was unresponsive shows the process continuously polling the Wayland socket (epoll_wait / recvmsg loop) without blocking or deadlocking, suggesting the event loop remains active but input events are no longer being processed at the application level.

nodes.title: [Wayland/Ozone] Per-window input freeze — events received on socket but not dispatched to affected window
nodes.body:
### Description

When running Electron (via VSCode) on native Wayland with the COSMIC compositor, individual windows intermittently and permanently lose all mouse and keyboard input. The window continues to render normally — buffer updates are composited, animations play, terminal output scrolls — but the window accepts zero input. No recovery is possible; the affected window must be closed.

Other Electron/VSCode windows of the same process remain fully functional. The freeze is per-window, not per-process or per-session.

### Key diagnostic finding

During an active freeze, I ran `strace` on the Electron browser process (PID 12219) for 15 seconds, tracing `recvmsg`, `sendmsg`, `read`, `write`, `poll`, `ppoll`, `epoll_wait`.

**The Wayland socket (fd 48) is actively receiving events:**

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Total strace lines (15s) | 9,746 |
| `recvmsg(48, ...)` calls | 3,272 |
| `sendmsg(48, ...)` calls | 154 |
| Dominant payload size | 28 bytes (1,169 calls) — matches `wl_pointer.motion` |
| Other payloads | 24B (146), 60B (139), 8B (132), 32B (40), 52B (4) |

The compositor IS sending Wayland events to the client's socket, and the Electron browser process IS reading them via `recvmsg()`. The browser process's main thread is in `ppoll()` (not blocked/stuck). Yet the affected window receives zero input.

This strongly suggests the bug is in the Ozone/Wayland input dispatch path — somewhere between reading the Wayland wire messages and routing them to the correct `wl_surface`/`BrowserWindow`.

### Reproduction

- **Not deterministic** — happens randomly, sometimes after minutes, sometimes after hours
- **Trigger**: Unknown. No specific action triggers it. Not correlated with drag-and-drop, focus changes, or fullscreen transitions
- **Frequency**: Multiple times per day across two different machines
- **Workaround**: `--ozone-platform=x11` (XWayland) eliminates the issue entirely

### What was ruled out

- **Not a compositor-wide issue**: Other windows (including other VSCode windows from the same process) continue to work
- **Not a GPU/rendering issue**: No dmesg errors, no GPU crashes, rendering continues in the frozen window
- **Not VSCode extensions**: No extension host crashes or errors correlated with freezes
- **Not VSCode's unresponsive detector**: `CodeWindow: detected unresponsive` does not fire because the renderer heartbeat passes (rendering works, only input is lost)
- **Not the compositor refusing events**: strace proves `recvmsg()` on the Wayland socket succeeds with meaningful payloads

### Environment

- **Electron**: 39.3.0 (bundled with VSCode 1.109.2, Chromium ~134)
- **Compositor**: COSMIC (cosmic-comp 1.0.0, Smithay-based)
- **GPU**: AMD Radeon RX 7900 XT (dGPU) + AMD Granite Ridge iGPU (Radeon Graphics)
- **Kernel**: 6.19.0-cachyos-lto
- **OS**: NixOS (x86_64-linux)
- **Tested on**: Two machines (atlas: Ryzen 9950X + RX 7900 XT, nomad: laptop with AMD iGPU)

### Process state during freeze

```
State: S (sleeping)
Threads: 45
Wchan: do_sys_poll
Main stack: do_sys_poll → __se_sys_ppoll → do_syscall_64
```

The main thread is in `ppoll()` waiting for events — the normal idle state. It is not deadlocked or stuck.

### strace excerpt (during active freeze, mouse moving over frozen window)

```
18:23:13.888284 recvmsg(48, {msg_name=NULL, ..., iov_len=1528}, ...) = 28 <0.000012>
18:23:13.888421 recvmsg(48, ...) = -1 EAGAIN
18:23:13.890119 recvmsg(48, {msg_name=NULL, ..., iov_len=1500}, ...) = 28 <0.000007>
18:23:13.890142 recvmsg(48, ...) = -1 EAGAIN
18:23:13.893148 recvmsg(48, {msg_name=NULL, ..., iov_len=1472}, ...) = 28 <0.000006>
18:23:13.893167 recvmsg(48, ...) = -1 EAGAIN
18:23:13.895149 recvmsg(48, {msg_name=NULL, ..., iov_len=1444}, ...) = 28 <0.000006>
18:23:13.895168 recvmsg(48, ...) = -1 EAGAIN
18:23:13.897182 recvmsg(48, {msg_name=NULL, ..., iov_len=1416}, ...) = 28 <0.000009>
18:23:13.897231 recvmsg(48, ...) = -1 EAGAIN
```

Rapid stream of 28-byte messages at ~2ms intervals — consistent with wl_pointer.motion events while moving the mouse over the frozen window.

### Related issues

- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/221961 — Nearly identical symptoms ("VSCode stops responding to mouse inputs after being unfocused"), closed as stale without resolution. Was assigned to `@deepak1556`.

### Electron Version

Electron v39.2.7

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Linux mace.inner.sanctum 6.18.9-200.fc43.x86_64 #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Fri Feb  6 21:43:09 UTC 2026 x86_64 GNU/Linux

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

Yes

### Expected Behavior

Typing Unicode characters outside the BMP (e.g. U+1F448 👈, U+1F91F 🤟) via keyboard input should insert the correct Unicode character, as provided by the Wayland input system (UTF-8 text).

### Actual Behavior

When typing certain non-BMP Unicode characters via keyboard input, the resulting character is incorrect and appears truncated:
        Intended: U+1F448 (👈)
        Actual: U+F448 ()
    This pattern is consistent for characters in the U+1Fxxx range, which appear to be truncated to U+Fxxx.
    The issue only occurs with direct keyboard input.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

I’m using Signal Desktop 7.89.0 (Flatpak from Flathub), which bundles Electron internally. I got the version from `flatpak run --command=sh org.signal.Signal -c 'cat /app/Signal/signal-desktop' | strings | grep -i "electron v" | head`. I hope that's what you needed.
However, I have reproduced the same behavior in a standalone Chromium build (RPM, not Flatpak), so this does not appear to be specific to Signal.
---
I investigated this using wev on Wayland and confirmed that the system is producing correct UTF-8 input.

Example:

```
sym: U1F448 (16905288), utf8: '👈'
sym: U1F91F (16906527), utf8: '🤟'
```

This indicates:

- XKB is correctly configured
- libxkbcommon is producing correct Unicode
- Wayland is delivering correct UTF-8 text

Despite this, Electron-based applications appear to ignore the provided UTF-8 and instead derive characters from the keysym, resulting in incorrect truncated codepoints (e.g. U+1F448 → U+F448).

Additional observations:

- Clipboard paste produces correct characters
- Compose sequences produce correct characters
- Only direct key input is affected

This suggests a keysym-to-character conversion path that does not correctly handle non-BMP Unicode.

---
This is my first bug report ever. I hope I did this correctly. I consulted ChatGPT to help me find where and how to tell someone about this. I’m here in good faith, I care about getting this right, and I’m open to correction.

### Expected Behavior

It should be possible to initialize a child window with a specific `zoomFactor` using the `overrideBrowserWindowOptions` object returned from a window open handler.

### Actual Behavior

Given this window open handler:
``` typescript
mainWindow.webContents.setWindowOpenHandler(() => ({
  action: 'allow',
  overrideBrowserWindowOptions: {
    webPreferences: {
      zoomFactor: 2
    }
  }
}))
```
the specified `zoomFactor` doesn't seem to have any effect. Calling `webContents.setZoomFactor()` in `did-create-window` also doesn't work; it seems necessary to wait for a later event like `did-finish-load`.

### Additional Information

In the test app, opening a window with `window.open()` uses the current zoom level, while opening one with `new BrowserWindow()` uses the zoom level specified in the constructor options.

Note that after going through the `new BrowserWindow()` path or setting the zoom level manually, the `window.open()` window will continue to use the updated zoom level (so it's not resetting the `zoomLevel` to default, just ignoring it).

nodes.title: Fuse to disable all Node.js flags
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

For security purposes, we should have a fuse to disable all Node.js flags in production applications.

The more [Node.js flags](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/command-line-switches#nodejs-flags) we expose, the higher the risk. In production apps, you'd usually want to disable all Node.js flags anyways.

### Proposed Solution

Add a fuse to disable all Node.js flags.

Similar to the [`nodeCliInspect` fuse](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/fuses#nodecliinspect), but for _all_ handling of Node.js flags.

Implementation idea: make [`IsAllowedOption`](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/8b057176618af9a47afed2a2e869932ebfc9093f/shell/common/node_bindings.cc#L404) always return false when the fuse is flipped.

### Alternatives Considered

- Not adding any Node.js flags to Electron at all. However, those flags can make development easier.
- Changing the existing `nodeCliInspect` fuse.

### Additional Information

Idea from https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/49711#pullrequestreview-3822516057.
